Week 40, 2026

Training programs

This is a weekly newsletter that lists newly announced training programs addressing existential risk from AI. Visit AISafety.com/training for the full directory of upcoming programs.

Next week, this newsletter moves off Substack and splits in two: "AI Safety Events" from events@news.aisafety.com and "AI Safety Training" from training@news.aisafety.com. They'll also look much nicer than this one.

If you get this by email, there's nothing you need to do: we'll move you over. Rather not come along? Unsubscribe below before 7 October and we won't move you. Each newsletter will have its own unsubscribe link, so you can keep one and drop the other. If either lands in spam or Promotions, move it to your inbox and it'll stay there.

Reading this in the Substack app? Sign up at AISafety.com/events and AISafety.com/training from 8 October (not yet!) to get the new emails. We'll send out a reminder.

Issue #24, 2026

Funding

This newsletter lists new and closing-soon funding opportunities for addressing existential risk from AI. Visit AISafety.com/funding for the full list of funders in AI safety.

Closing in the next two weeks
Corrigibility Research Fund
Awards grants and prizes for corrigibility research.
Consider applying if: you need around $5k–$35k for corrigibility research that’s compatible with mainstream ML and useful to the people building AI systems. There’s no location or affiliation requirement.
 Applications close 31 Oct 2026
 Who can apply: individuals, nonprofits
 Grant size: Typically $5k – $35k
Always open

The main go-to funders – we include them every time as a reminder. See AISafety.com/funding for the full list.

Lightcone Commons
Grantmaking platform coordinating large-scale philanthropy in quarterly rounds.
 Applications on a rolling basis
 Who can apply: individuals, nonprofits, for-profits, universities
